extracted.intended_audience: general public and news consumers (wire subscribers, newspaper readers)
extracted.subtask_description: An Associated Press wartime roundup dispatch reporting frontline operations, air strikes, movements and casualty figures from the Korean War; intended to inform readers and summarize rapidly changing military events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of unconfirmed enemy claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Such reports are handled separately, or bracketed into roundup stories and clearly identified as an unconfirmed enemy claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explains that exaggerated casualty reports have frequently come from enemy sources (e.g., the North Korean radio at Pyongyang) and gives the example of a Red broadcast claiming '700 Americans killed and 200 captured.' Editorial practice shown: separate or bracket such enemy-origin claims in reporting and clearly label them as unconfirmed enemy claims so readers understand their status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify scope of reported casualty figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The figures ... were confined to ground fighting and did not include ... (as noted when MacArthur's headquarters placed U.S. casualties at 488: 'This included 42 killed in action, 150 wounded and 256 missing. The figures ... were confined to ground fighting and did not include ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing casualty totals, specify what the numbers cover (e.g., confined to ground fighting) and note exclusions or limitations so readers are not misled. The article illustrates providing breakdowns (killed, wounded, missing) and explicitly stating scope and any potential sources of distortion (e.g., missing personnel who may have lost touch with units).
